title: Excellence is preserved by finite type algebras and localization
statement: Let $R$ be an excellent commutative ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], let $A$ be a finite type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $S\subseteq A$ be a multiplicative subset ($1\in S$ and $st\in S$ for $s,t\in S$). Then the localization $S^{-1}A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is excellent. In particular $A$ is excellent by taking $S=\{1\}$.

proof.text: By [def-exc-excellent-ring], $R$ is Noetherian, a G-ring, J-2, and universally catenary. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to $R\to A$ to obtain Noetherianity of $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] to the same finite type map to obtain that $A$ is a G-ring. Both applications use exactly the given finite type hypothesis; neither requires that $R\to A$ be injective.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent, finite type case; Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring; algebra.tex Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence

proof.text: For any finite type $A$-algebra $T$, choose finite algebra generators $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $A$ over $R$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ of $T$ over $A$. Substitution of polynomial expressions shows that the images of the $a_i$, together with the $t_j$, generate $T$ over $R$, by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Since $R$ is J-2 and universally catenary, [def-exc-excellent-ring] therefore says that the regular locus of $T$ is open and that $T$ is catenary. As $T$ was arbitrary, $A$ is J-2 and universally catenary. Together with step 1 this makes $A$ excellent.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent, first proof sentence; Tag 07P7, definition-J; algebra.tex Tag 00NL, definition-universally-catenary

proof.text: Put $B=S^{-1}A$ and let $\lambda:A\to B$ send $a$ to $a/1$. The fraction construction of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] in the case of the module $A$ supplies a commutative ring, sends every $s\in S$ to a unit, represents every element as $\lambda(a)\lambda(s)^{-1}$, and says that $\lambda(a)=0$ implies $sa=0$ for some $s\in S$. Thus all localization hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] hold; with the Noetherianity from step 1 it makes $B$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, localization assertion; Section 00CM, section-localization, fraction formulas

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, let $\mathfrak p=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. By parts (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], the map $e:A_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{\mathfrak q}$, $a/t\mapsto\lambda(a)/\lambda(t)$, is an isomorphism carrying the maximal ideal onto the maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-ring-equiv] at these maximal ideals to obtain an isomorphism $E:(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(B_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ commuting with the canonical completion maps. The map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ is regular because $A$ is a G-ring, by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. The commuting square with vertical isomorphisms $e,E$ satisfies exactly the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-map-ring-equiv], so $B_{\mathfrak q}\to(B_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is regular. Since $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary and $B$ is Noetherian by step 3, [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] makes $B$ a G-ring.

source.place: Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, opening proof sentence on localization; Tag 07GH, definition-G-ring; algebra.tex Tag 00C9, item-localization-localization

proof.text: Fix any finite type $B$-algebra $C$, with generators $c_1,\ldots,c_m$ as in [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Inside $C$ let $D$ be the subring of polynomial expressions in the $c_i$ with coefficients in the image of $A$. It is a finite type $A$-algebra, with those same generators. Let $S_D$ be the image of $S$ in $D$; its elements are units in $C$, since the structure map factors through $B$. The formula $d/s\mapsto d\,s^{-1}$ defines a homomorphism $S_D^{-1}D\to C$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]: the relation $u(td-se)=0$ implies equality of the two fractions after multiplying by the unit $ust$. This map is injective because $d\,s^{-1}=0$ implies $d=0$ in the subring $D$. It is surjective: express an element of $C$ as a polynomial in the $c_i$ with finitely many coefficients $a_\alpha/s_\alpha\in B$, and put $s=\prod_\alpha s_\alpha\in S$. That polynomial equals $d/\lambda_C(s)$, where $d=\sum_\alpha \lambda_C(a_\alpha)\prod_{\beta\ne\alpha}\lambda_C(s_\beta)c^\alpha\in D$ and $\lambda_C:A\to C$ is the structure map. Thus $C\cong S_D^{-1}D$ by this explicit map. No finite-presentation or injectivity hypothesis on $A\to C$ was used.

source.place: Tag 00NJ, lemma-localization-catenary, finite type localization model in its proof; explicit image-subalgebra and common-denominator argument

proof.text: For the arbitrary $C$ and $D$ of step 5, both rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]: apply it to the finite type maps $A\to D$ and $B\to C$, using the Noetherianity of $A$ and $B$ from steps 1 and 3. Now $D$ has open regular locus because $A$ is J-2, by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. The canonical map $h:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is continuous by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding], applied to the localization isomorphism of step 5. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] identifies $C_{\mathfrak q}$ with $D_{h(\mathfrak q)}$ for each prime $\mathfrak q$. Regular locality is invariant under this ring isomorphism directly from [def-weil-regular-scheme]: it bijects ideals and their finite generating families, carries the unique maximal ideal to the unique maximal ideal, and bijects prime chains, preserving their lengths and hence Krull dimension. Consequently $\operatorname{Reg}(C)=h^{-1}(\operatorname{Reg}(D))$ is open. Since this holds for every finite type $B$-algebra $C$, $B$ is J-2. The argument only uses continuity; it does not assert that the image of an arbitrary localization is open.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent, omitted localization assertion for J-2, supplied here from Tag 07P7, definition-J; algebra.tex Tags 00E3, lemma-spec-localization, and 00KU, definition-regular-local

proof.text: The finite type $A$-algebra $D$ in step 5 is catenary because $A$ is universally catenary, by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. By part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], contraction identifies primes of $C$ with primes of $D$ disjoint from $S_D$, and extension is its inverse. Both preserve inclusion, since contraction and the formation of the ideal generated by an image preserve inclusion. If $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ are the contractions of two primes of $C$, every prime of $D$ between them avoids $S_D$ because it is contained in $\mathfrak q$, which avoids $S_D$. Hence the entire interval of primes is preserved, not only its endpoints. Every finite chain corresponds to a chain of the same length; a chain is saturated on one side exactly when it is saturated on the other, since any insertable prime lies in this interval. The bound on finite chain lengths and the common length of saturated chains for $D$ therefore give the same two conditions for $C$. Thus $C$ is catenary. As $C$ was arbitrary and $B$ is Noetherian, $B$ is universally catenary.

source.place: Tag 00NJ, lemma-localization-catenary, proof; Tags 00NI, definition-catenary, and 00NL, definition-universally-catenary

proof.text: Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 respectively give Noetherianity, the G-ring property, J-2 and universal catenarity for $B=S^{-1}A$. These are exactly the conditions for excellence in [def-exc-excellent-ring], proving the principal assertion. Step 2 already proves the final assertion that $A$ is excellent. Equivalently, for $S=\{1\}$ the mutually inverse maps $a/1\mapsto a$ and $a\mapsto a/1$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] identify $S^{-1}A$ with $A$. No condition that $S$ avoid zero is needed: if $0\in S$, then $B=0$ by the fraction relation, there are no primes, and every $B$-algebra is zero, so the primewise and open-locus conditions used above are vacuous.
